name: A Two-Component Shadow Split Determines an Edge Factorization
statement: Let a simplicial complex $\Sigma\subseteq2^F$ contain every singleton and have connected two-face graph. If deleting coordinate $e$ leaves exactly two graph components $F_1,F_2$, put $\Sigma_i=\Sigma\cap2^{F_i\cup\{e\}}$. Every ample realization of $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing ample realizations of the two $\Sigma_i$, choosing and identifying oriented $e$-edges, embedding their exclusive blocks disjointly, and applying a cube translation. Every output has one separating $e$-edge, which recovers the two convex pieces up to interchange and simultaneous edge reversal. The pc-minimal obstructions among these realizations are exactly the two-piece data satisfying the separating-edge obstruction criterion.
proof: No face of $\Sigma$ meets both exclusive blocks, so the two subcomplexes meet only in the empty face and $\{e\}$. The edge-glued realization has shadow $\Sigma$ and cardinality $|\Sigma|$, hence is ample. Connectivity of the two subgraphs makes each piece two-connected and its complement of the chosen edge connected; crossing-graph separator recovery then makes the identified edge unique. Conversely, that theorem recovers the edge and its convex blocks from any realization. Projection onto each block plus $e$ recovers a realization of $\Sigma_i$, and normalizing the edge recovers the construction up to the stated symmetries.
